title: Safe Work Procedure — Concrete Pour
summary: Controls for deck and column concrete placement with tower crane buckets and vibrators.
purpose: Prevent struck-by, fall, and pour-related incidents during concrete placement.
scope: Applies to all Helix crews placing concrete on elevated decks, columns, and walls using tower crane or pump.
ppe: Hard hat, safety glasses, hi-vis vest
Fall protection when within 2 m of an open edge
steps: Hold pre-pour briefing — review FLHA, lift path, radio channel, and stop-work criteria.
Confirm formwork is inspected, braced, and signed off before placement starts.
Verify edge protection, covers, and exclusion zones under the lift path.
Confirm crane, bucket, and vibrators are in service; tag out damaged cords.
Use designated signal person; maintain continuous radio contact on blind pours.
Place concrete in controlled lifts; do not overload forms or decks.
Keep vibrator operators rotated; keep cords clear of traffic and edges.
Clean splash from skin immediately; wash PPE and tools after pour.
Re-inspect rails and covers before stripping or next trade access.
emergency: Stop pour and lower load if radio contact is lost
Muster at posted site muster point for medical / rescue
Flush concrete from eyes/skin with clean water for 15 minutes

title: Safe Work Procedure — Formwork & Stripping
summary: Erecting, bracing, and stripping Peri/Doka formwork on elevated levels.
purpose: Control collapse, struck-by, and fall hazards during formwork erection and stripping.
scope: All formwork carpenters, apprentices, and labourers erecting or stripping wall, column, and deck forms.
ppe: Hearing protection when using impact tools
hazards: Pinch points on clamps and wedges
steps: Review manufacturer instructions and project SJP before starting.
Inspect panels, walers, ties, and braces — remove damaged components.
Establish exclusion zones below stripping areas; post a spotter.
Install temporary edge protection before removing permanent rails where required.
Brace sequentially; never leave free-standing panels unsecured.
Use rated lifting gear for panel hops; no free-hand guiding under suspended loads.
Strip only after concrete strength and supervisor release.
Lower materials by controlled means — no dropping or free-falling forms.
Housekeep nails, wedges, and ties immediately; restore rails before leaving bay.
emergency: Evacuate bay and notify supervisor if bracing movement is observed
Do not enter under partially stripped forms
Call site emergency contact for entrapment or crush injuries

title: Safe Work Procedure — Yard Operations
summary: Material handling, forklift, and laydown controls at the Helix yard.
purpose: Prevent vehicle/pedestrian conflicts and material-handling injuries in the yard.
scope: Yard crew, deliveries, and any field worker picking up or returning materials/equipment.
steps: Sign in at yard office; confirm task and travel path with yard supervisor.
Stay in marked pedestrian walkways; make eye contact with equipment operators.
Inspect forklift / telehandler before use; report deficiencies.
Stack materials within rated heights; band or chock as required.
Use tag lines on suspended loads; never walk under a load.
Secure loads before leaving the yard; close gates and tag incomplete stacks.
emergency: Stop equipment and clear zone for any tip / spill
Use yard muster point by the main gate
Report all near misses to yard supervisor the same day

title: Safe Work Procedure — Tower Crane Operations
summary: Daily setup, communication, and shut-down for tower crane work.
purpose: Maintain controlled lifts and clear communication between operator, rigger, and signal person.
scope: Tower crane operators, riggers, and signal persons on Helix high-rise sites.
ppe: Fall protection in cabin access / climb
hazards: Blind lifts and lost radio contact
steps: Complete daily crane inspection and log before first lift.
Confirm radio channel, call signs, and emergency stop protocol.
Review lift plan / critical lift plan for the day’s work.
Check wind speed against OEM chart; suspend lifts if limits exceeded.
Maintain exclusion zones; use dedicated signal person for blind picks.
Never leave a suspended load unattended.
Weathervane and secure crane per OEM at end of shift or high wind.
emergency: If radio fails — stop, sound horn pattern, wait for visual signal
Lower load if safe; otherwise hold and call supervisor
Evacuate swing radius for mechanical failure

title: Safe Work Procedure — Working at Heights
summary: Fall protection selection, tie-off, and rescue readiness above 3 m or open edges.
purpose: Eliminate unprotected falls and ensure rescue capability on elevated work.
scope: Any Helix worker exposed to a fall hazard of 3 m or more, or working near an open edge.
ppe: Shock-absorbing lanyard or SRL as required
Hard hat with chin strap where required
steps: Inspect harness, lanyard/SRL, and connectors before each use.
Prefer collective protection (rails/covers) over personal fall arrest.
Select rated anchors; maintain 100% tie-off when exposed.
Control swing fall; keep free-fall distance within equipment rating.
Cover or guard floor openings immediately when created.
Confirm rescue plan and equipment are available before starting work.
Tag and remove defective fall gear from service.
emergency: Activate site rescue plan immediately after fall arrest
Do not leave a suspended worker unattended
Call emergency services if rescue cannot be completed promptly

title: Safe Job Procedure — Rigging & Signalling
summary: Step-by-step job procedure for preparing, signalling, and landing suspended loads.
purpose: Standardize how Helix crews rig and signal lifts so every pick follows the same safe sequence.
scope: Riggers and signal persons supporting tower or mobile crane lifts on Helix projects.
steps: Review lift plan, load weight, and radius with operator before the pick.
Inspect slings, shackles, hooks, and tag lines; reject damaged gear.
Confirm centre of gravity; choke or basket hitch as specified.
Clear the travel path and landing zone; post barricades if needed.
Establish who has radio control; confirm test call with operator.
Take slack slowly; stop if load shifts or gear binds.
Use tag lines — never guide a load with hands under or against it.
Land on stable blocking; wait for slack before disconnecting.
Store gear neatly; report any shock-loaded or damaged equipment.
emergency: Emergency stop: continuous radio call “STOP STOP STOP” + horn
If load becomes unstable — clear zone, do not approach
Notify supervisor and log near miss before next pick

title: Safe Job Procedure — Blind Lift Radio Protocol
summary: Radio call sequence and stop criteria for lifts without continuous visual contact.
purpose: Keep blind lifts controlled through disciplined radio protocol and clear stop-work triggers.
scope: Any lift where the operator cannot see the load, landing zone, or signal person continuously.
ppe: Assigned radio on Ch 3 — Tower Ops
Hi-vis for all personnel in the lift zone
Backup air horn at landing zone
steps: Confirm this is a blind lift in the pre-lift briefing; name primary and backup signal person.
Radio check: operator ↔ signal person ↔ supervisor before first movement.
Use standard call signs (e.g., “TC-1”, “Deck Signal”).
Call every movement: “Up on load”, “Swing left”, “Down slow”, “Hold”.
Operator repeats critical commands before moving.
If radio is garbled or silent for one attempt — STOP and sound horn.
Do not resume until two-way contact and visual spotter are restored.
Log blind lift completion and any holds in the daily crane notes.
emergency: Lost contact = immediate hold; do not guess the next move
Clear swing radius if load position is unknown
Escalate to superintendent after any uncontrolled drift
references: Toolbox Talk — Blind lift radio protocol

title: Safe Job Procedure — Wall Form Stripping
summary: Ordered sequence for stripping Peri wall forms without collapse or falling materials.
purpose: Provide a job-specific sequence so stripping crews remove forms in a controlled order.
scope: Crews stripping vertical Peri wall forms on Helix projects after pour release.
steps: Confirm concrete release and supervisor authorization to strip.
Barricade below; assign a spotter — no entry under the wall.
Install / verify temporary edge protection on the working side.
Loosen ties in the planned sequence; support panel before final release.
Attach crane / forklift gear before free-standing the panel.
Walk the panel clear; land on designated blocking.
Restore rails and covers before opening the bay to other trades.
Stage stripped materials for return to yard; housekeep continuously.
emergency: If panel kicks — clear zone, do not attempt to catch
Stop work and reassess bracing after any unexpected movement
Treat crush injuries as site emergency — call posted contact

title: Safe Job Procedure — MEWP / Scissor Lift Use
summary: Pre-use checks and operating steps for scissor lifts and boom lifts on site.
purpose: Ensure only trained operators use MEWPs and that ground conditions and fall controls are verified.
scope: Workers operating Helix MEWPs for install, inspection, or access tasks.
ppe: Harness / lanyard as required by MEWP type
hazards: Tip-over on soft or sloping ground
steps: Confirm operator training and machine suitability for the task.
Inspect MEWP, controls, gates, and emergency lowering — log defects.
Check ground bearing, holes, and overhead clearance.
Barricade travel / work zone; use a spotter in congested areas.
Wear required fall protection; keep feet on the platform floor.
Do not exceed rated capacity or use as a crane.
Lower, isolate, and secure machine at end of use.
emergency: Use ground-level emergency lowering if operator is incapacitated
Do not climb out of an elevated platform except in extreme rescue
Tag out defective MEWPs immediately

title: Safe Work Assessment — High-Rise Deck
summary: Assessment of residual risk for high-rise deck pours and formwork.
purpose: Document residual risks and required controls for elevated deck work.
scope: Oceanview Tower and similar high-rise deck operations.
ppe: As per FLHA and Working at Heights SWP
steps: Review assessment with crew at start of deck cycle.
Confirm controls from linked SWPs/SJPs are in place.
Update assessment when means/methods change.
emergency: Follow site ERP

title: Lift Plan — Tower Crane Standard Lifts
summary: Standard lift parameters, radii, and communication for routine tower crane picks.
purpose: Define approved methods for non-critical tower crane lifts.
scope: Routine material and formwork hops within charted capacity.
steps: Confirm load weight and radius within chart.
Use SJP — Rigging & Signalling for the pick sequence.
Escalate to Critical Lift Plan when criteria are met.
emergency: Follow Crane Ops SWP emergency steps

title: Critical Lift Plan — Blind Column Pours
summary: Enhanced controls for blind column pours exceeding standard lift criteria.
purpose: Mandate extra planning, supervision, and radio protocol for critical blind pours.
scope: Column pours where operator vision is obstructed or load exceeds 75% chart.
steps: Hold critical lift meeting with named roles.
Follow Blind Lift Radio Protocol SJP without deviation.
Superintendent must be on channel for the pour.
emergency: Hold lift and muster if any stop criteria are met

title: Emergency Response Plan
summary: Site emergency contacts, muster points, and response roles.
purpose: Provide a single emergency response reference for all Helix sites.
scope: All Helix workers and visitors on active projects.
steps: Know your muster point and emergency contact before starting work.
Call site emergency number, then 911 if needed.
Account for crew at muster; do not re-enter until cleared.
emergency: Follow posted project emergency contact and muster point

title: Site Orientation Package
summary: Mandatory orientation topics before a worker starts on a Helix site.
purpose: Ensure every worker knows site rules, hazards, reporting, and emergency procedures.
scope: All new and transferred workers before first task.
ppe: Site-minimum PPE before entering work areas
steps: Complete orientation checklist with supervisor.
Tour muster point, first aid, and wash stations.
Sign acknowledgement before starting work.
emergency: Covered in orientation — see ERP

title: Toolbox Talk — Blind Lift Radio Protocol
summary: Today’s toolbox talk aligned with the Blind Lift Radio Protocol SJP.
purpose: Refresh crew awareness before shifts involving blind picks.
scope: Crew B and Crew C before first lift today.
steps: Review SJP — Blind Lift Radio Protocol highlights.
Confirm channel and call signs for the day.
Collect acknowledgement signatures on the crew roster.
emergency: Stop work if radio protocol cannot be maintained

title: Manufacturer Instructions — Peri / Doka Systems
summary: OEM erection and stripping guidance for formwork systems in use.
purpose: Ensure formwork is assembled per manufacturer requirements.
scope: Formwork crews using Peri or Doka systems on Helix projects.
steps: Use only compatible components for the system.
Follow OEM brace and tie spacing.
Do not modify components without engineering approval.
emergency: Stop and get engineering input if system does not match drawings
